content: The following individuals participated fully in the described activities: Koleka Mlisana from the National Health Laboratory Service in South Africa. Lori Newman from the National Institutes of Health in the USA. Annex 2: Declarations of Interests and Management of Conflicts of Interest The following declarations and management plans were noted: 1. Catherine Ngugui (Ministry of Health, Kenya): Received research support from the Global Antibiotic Research and Development Partnership (GARDP), the Drugs for Neglected Diseases Initiative (DNDi), and the Ministry of Health for a study on the prevalence of Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae infections among pregnant women and key populations in Kenya. The funding amounted to $40,000 and ceased in 2022. No active conflicts of interest were reported. Full participation was confirmed. 2. Remco Peters (University of Pretoria, South Africa): Received research support from the Foundation for Innovative New Diagnostics (FIND) for the evaluation of a lateral flow assay for point-of-care detection of Neisseria gonorrhoeae, with funding amounting to $645,000. Additional support was received from the South African Medical Research Council for a project on antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and molecular typing of Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Full participation was confirmed. 3. Melanie Taylor (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, USA): Full participation was confirmed. Updated Recommendations Updated recommendations were provided for the treatment of Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, and syphilis. Additionally, new recommendations were introduced regarding syphilis testing and partner services.
